6.1 Scoring rules
6.1.1 Scoring rule
Definition: A scoring rule is any extended real-valued function S : Q × Ω → R where Q is a family
of probability distributions over the space Ω, such that S(Q, ·) is Q-quasi-integrable for all Q ∈ Q.
Output of the function S(Q, y) represents the loss or penalty when the forecast Q ∈ Q is issued and
the observation y ∈ Ω is realized.
Sources:
• Bálint Mucsányi, Michael Kirchhof, Elisa Nguyen, Alexander Rubinstein, Seong Joon Oh (2023):
“Proper/Strictly Proper Scoring Rule”; in: Trustworthy Machine Learning; URL: https://trustworthyml.
io/; DOI: 10.48550/arXiv.2310.08215.
• Wikipedia (2024): “Scoring rule”; in: Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia, retrieved on 2024-02-28;
URL: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scoring_rule.
